sourceAgencies: NJ Division of Pensions and Benefits (SHBP / SEHBP)
Wayne Township Public Schools User-Friendly Budget

overview.percentageOfCombinedBudgets: 21.3% of all public spending in Wayne Township goes directly to employee health insurance and pensions

healthcarePlans.providers: Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield / SEHBP & Municipal Health Plan

primaryPlans.planName: NJ Educators Health Plan (NJEHP / Chapter 44) & Garden State Plan
primaryPlans.description: Caps employee premium contributions as a percentage of base salary (1.7% to 7.2%), shifting annual double-digit healthcare premium spikes onto local property taxes.
Nationwide PPO network with low copays and low deductibles for grandfathered municipal employees.
Comprehensive drug formulary covering retail, mail-order, and specialty biologics with taxpayers subsidizing over 85% of costs.

rules.employeeContribution: 10% to 35% of premium based on salary
rules.taxpayerContribution: 65% to 90% of total family premium ($24,000 - $32,000/yr subsidy)
rules.note: For an employee with a $35,000 family health plan, Wayne Township taxpayers subsidize ~$24,500+ every year.
Because employee share is tied to salary rather than premium cost, 100% of health insurance rate hikes fall on the property tax levy.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Multi-million dollar ongoing retiree health expenditure
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Employees retiring with 25+ years of pensionable service receive employer-paid health benefits in retirement.

retirementAndLeaveBenefits.benefitName: Unused Sick & Vacation Leave Retirement Payouts
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.taxpayerImpact: Lump-sum retirement payouts funded from budget reserves
retirementAndLeaveBenefits.details: Grandfathered veteran employees retain contractual rights to cash out accumulated unused sick and vacation days upon retirement.
